          41	/// <summary>
          42	/// EcoClean Environmental Biocleavage &amp; Mineralization Knowledge Engine.
          43	/// Traverses the molecular graph of target pollutants, retrieves topological Bond Dissociation
          44	/// Energies (BDE), and constructs standard enzymatic and electrochemical catalytic mineralization pathways.
          45	/// </summary>
          46	public static class EcoCleanEngine
          47	{
          48	    /// <summary>
          49	    /// Computes the complete dynamic catalytic biocleavage and mineralization cascade for any target compound.
          50	    /// </summary>
          51	    /// <param name="input">Pollutant formula, common acronym, or SMILES string.</param>
          52	    /// <returns>Step-by-step degradation cascade and predicted mineralization efficiency.</returns>
          53	    public static EcoCleanDegradationResult SolveDegradationCascade(string input)
          54	    {
          55	        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(input);
          56
          57	        Molecule molecule;
          58	        string trimmed = input.Trim();
          59
          60	        if (Molecule.TryParse(trimmed, trimmed, out var mol) || Molecule.TryParseSmiles(trimmed, trimmed, out mol))
          61	        {
          62	            molecule = mol;
          63	        }
          64	        else
          65	        {
          66	            // Check parts (e.g. "PFOA C8HF15O2")
          67	            Molecule? foundMol = null;
          68	            var parts = trimmed.Split([' ', ',', ';'], StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
          69	            foreach (var part in parts)
          70	            {
          71	                if (Molecule.TryParse(part, part, out var pMol) || Molecule.TryParseSmiles(part, part, out pMol))
          72	                {
          73	                    foundMol = pMol;
          74	                    break;
          75	                }
          76	            }
          77
          78	            molecule = foundMol ?? (trimmed.Contains("PFOA", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
          79	                ? Molecule.Parse("C8HF15O2", "PFOA")
          80	                : Molecule.Parse("CH4", "Pollutant"));
          81	        }
          82
          83	        var elements = molecule.Atoms.Select(a => a.Element.Symbol).Distinct().ToHashSet();
          84	        var fgs = molecule.GetFunctionalGroups().Select(f => f.ToString()).ToHashSet(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
          85	        var steps = new List<CleavageStep>();
          86
          87	        string pollutantClass;
          88	        double halfLife;
          89
          90	        // Calculate dynamic Bond Dissociation Energy (BDE) from molecular graph bonds
          91	        double primaryBde = 85.0;
          92	        double secondaryBde = 110.0;
          93
          94	        if (molecule.Bonds.Count > 0)
          95	        {
          96	            var bdes = molecule.Bonds.Select(b =>
          97	            {
          98	                string s1 = molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol;
          99	                string s2 = molecule.Atoms[b.Atom2Index].Element.Symbol;
         100	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "F") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "F")) return 116.0;
         101	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "Cl") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "Cl")) return 78.0;
         102	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "Br") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "Br")) return 66.0;
         103	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "O") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "O")) return b.Type == BondType.Double ? 179.0 : 86.0;
         104	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "N") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "N")) return 73.0;
         105	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "C") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "C")) return b.Type == BondType.Aromatic ? 102.0 : (b.Type == BondType.Double ? 146.0 : 83.0);
         106	                if ((s1 == "C" && s2 == "H") || (s2 == "C" && s1 == "H")) return 99.0;
         107	                if ((s1 == "P" && s2 == "O") || (s2 == "P" && s1 == "O")) return 88.0;
         108	                if ((s1 == "S" && s2 == "H") || (s2 == "S" && s1 == "H")) return 81.0;
         109	                return 80.0;
         110	            }).OrderBy(x => x).ToList();
         111
         112	            primaryBde = bdes.First();
         113	            secondaryBde = bdes.Last();
         114	        }
         115
         116	        // 1. Fluorinated Pollutants (PFAS / PFOA Forever Chemicals)
         117	        if (elements.Contains("F") || input.Contains("PFOA", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || input.Contains("PFAS", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
         118	        {
         119	            pollutantClass = "PFAS 'Forever Chemical' (Perfluoroalkyl Substance)";
         120	            halfLife = 1000.0;
         121
         122	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         123	                1,
         124	                "Terminal Carboxylate Decarboxylation (C-COOH)",
         125	                Math.Round(primaryBde, 1),
         126	                "Electrochemical Anodic Oxidation / UV-Sulfite Catalysis",
         127	                "Perfluoroalkyl Radical [CnF2n+1•]",
         128	                "Electron transfer induces homolytic decarboxylation to generate perfluoroalkyl radical."
         129	            ));
         130
         131	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         132	                2,
         133	                "Radical Hydroxylation & HF Elimination (C-F Cleavage)",
         134	                Math.Round(secondaryBde, 1),
         135	                "Microbial Dehalogenase / Hydroxyl Radical (•OH)",
         136	                "Perfluoroalkanol -> Perfluoroacyl Fluoride",
         137	                "Unstable perfluoroalcohol undergoes spontaneous α-elimination of Fluoride (F⁻)."
         138	            ));
         139
         140	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         141	                3,
         142	                "Iterative Chain Shortening Cascade (C_n -> C_n-1)",
         143	                105.0,
         144	                "Engineered Pseudomonas / Rhodococcus Biocatalyst",
         145	                "Short-chain carboxylates (TFA / Formate)",
         146	                "Sequential one-carbon iterative trimming down to inorganic CO₂ and benign F⁻ salts."
         147	            ));
         148	        }
         149	        // 2. Chlorinated / Brominated Xenobiotics (Pesticides, Organochlorides, PCBs, DDT)
         150	        else if (elements.Contains("Cl") || elements.Contains("Br"))
         151	        {
         152	            string halogen = elements.Contains("Cl") ? "Chlorine (Cl)" : "Bromine (Br)";
         153	            pollutantClass = $"Halogenated Persistent Organopollutant ({halogen})";
         154	            halfLife = 120.0;
         155
         156	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         157	                1,
         158	                $"Reductive Dehalogenation (C-{(elements.Contains("Cl") ? "Cl" : "Br")})",
         159	                Math.Round(primaryBde, 1),
         160	                "Anaerobic Dehalococcoides mccartyi / Vitamin B12 Catalysis",
         161	                "Dehalogenated Alkane / Aromatic Intermediate",
         162	                "Cobalamin-mediated electron transfer reduces carbon-halogen bond to halide anion."
         163	            ));
         164
         165	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         166	                2,
         167	                "Aerobic Dioxygenase Ring Fission",
         168	                74.0,
         169	                "Catechol 1,2-Dioxygenase Biocatalyst",
         170	                "cis,cis-Muconate Derivative",
         171	                "Intradiol oxygen insertion breaks aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold."
         172	            ));
         173	        }
         174	        // 3. Esters, Polymers & Microplastics (PET, PLA, Polyurethanes)
         175	        else if (fgs.Contains("Ester") || input.Contains("PET", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || input.Contains("Plastic", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
         176	        {
         177	            pollutantClass = "Microplastic / Synthetic Polyester Polymer (PET / PLA)";
         178	            halfLife = 450.0;
         179
         180	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         181	                1,
         182	                "Ester Backbone Hydrolysis (C(=O)-O)",
         183	                Math.Round(primaryBde, 1),
         184	                "Engineered PETase / Cutinase Enzyme (FAST-PETase)",
         185	                "Mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET)",
         186	                "Active-site Serine nucleophilic attack hydrolyzes ester bond at ambient 30°C."
         187	            ));
         188
         189	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         190	                2,
         191	                "Secondary Monomer Hydrolysis (MHETase)",
         192	                65.0,
         193	                "MHETase Enzyme",
         194	                "Terephthalic Acid (TPA) + Ethylene Glycol",
         195	                "Hydrolyzes monomer into recyclable raw building blocks."
         196	            ));
         197
         198	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         199	                3,
         200	                "Cellular Assimilation into Biopolymer",
         201	                52.0,
         202	                "Comamonas testosteroni / E. coli biocatalyst",
         203	                "Cellular ATP, CO₂, and H₂O",
         204	                "Complete enzymatic conversion into biodegradable PHA bioplastics."
         205	            ));
         206	        }
         207	        // 4. Organophosphates & Sulfur Contaminants (Nerve Agents, Pesticides)
         208	        else if (elements.Contains("P") || elements.Contains("S"))
         209	        {
         210	            pollutantClass = "Organophosphorus / Sulfur Contaminant";
         211	            halfLife = 15.0;
         212
         213	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         214	                1,
         215	                "Phosphoester / Thioester Bond Cleavage",
         216	                Math.Round(primaryBde, 1),
         217	                "Phosphotriesterase (PTE) Enzyme / Organophosphorus Hydrolase",
         218	                "Dialkylphosphate Intermediate",
         219	                "Active-site bimetallic zinc/zinc center coordinates water for rapid nucleophilic attack."
         220	            ));
         221
         222	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         223	                2,
         224	                "Phosphodiesterase Secondary Hydrolysis",
         225	                60.0,
         226	                "GpdQ Phosphodiesterase",
         227	                "Inorganic Orthophosphate",
         228	                "Cleaves remaining alkyl chains yielding non-toxic inorganic phosphate salts."
         229	            ));
         230	        }
         231	        // 5. General Organic Synthetic Pollutants & Hydrocarbons
         232	        else
         233	        {
         234	            pollutantClass = "Synthetic Hydrocarbon / Xenobiotic";
         235	            halfLife = 20.0;
         236
         237	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         238	                1,
         239	                "Oxidative Ring / Alkane Hydroxylation (C-H Activation)",
         240	                Math.Round(primaryBde, 1),
         241	                "Cytochrome P450 Monooxygenase / Laccase",
         242	                "Hydroxylated / Catecholic Intermediate",
         243	                "Oxygen insertion functionalizes inert C-H bonds for downstream cleavage."
         244	            ));
         245
         246	            steps.Add(new CleavageStep(
         247	                2,
         248	                "Aliphatic / Aromatic Carbon Cleavage (C-C fission)",
         249	                Math.Round(secondaryBde, 1),
         250	                "Catechol Dioxygenase / Baeyer-Villiger Monooxygenase",
         251	                "Aliphatic Dicarboxylic Acids",
         252	                "Oxidative cleavage breaks carbon-carbon backbone into cellular Krebs cycle nutrients."
         253	            ));
         254	        }
         255
         256	        // Build inorganic stoichiometric mass-conserved end products
         257	        var productList = new List<string>();
         258	        if (elements.Contains("F")) productList.Add("Fluoride (F⁻)");
         259	        if (elements.Contains("Cl")) productList.Add("Chloride (Cl⁻)");
         260	        if (elements.Contains("Br")) productList.Add("Bromide (Br⁻)");
         261	        if (elements.Contains("S")) productList.Add("Sulfate (SO₄²⁻)");
         262	        if (elements.Contains("P")) productList.Add("Phosphate (PO₄³⁻)");
         263	        if (elements.Contains("N")) productList.Add("Nitrate (NO₃⁻)");
         264	        productList.Add("CO₂");
         265	        productList.Add("H₂O");
         266
         267	        string endProducts = string.Join(" + ", productList) + " (100% Mineralized)";
         268	        double efficiency = Math.Round(99.0 + Math.Clamp(10.0 / secondaryBde, 0.2, 0.8), 1);
         269
         270	        return new EcoCleanDegradationResult(
         271	            molecule.ChemicalFormula,
         272	            pollutantClass,
         273	            halfLife,
         274	            efficiency,
         275	            steps,
         276	            endProducts
         277	        );
         278	    }
         279	}
           1	using Chemy.Core.Spatial;
           2
           3	namespace Chemy.Core.Physics;
           4
           5	/// <summary>
           6	/// Encapsulates the results of a 3D Cartesian molecular mechanics energy minimization run.
           7	/// </summary>
           8	/// <param name="Formula">Molecular formula.</param>
           9	/// <param name="InitialEnergyKcalPerMol">Potential energy prior to geometric relaxation (kcal/mol).</param>
          10	/// <param name="FinalEnergyKcalPerMol">Relaxed potential energy at local minimum (kcal/mol).</param>
          11	/// <param name="Iterations">Number of gradient descent iterations performed.</param>
          12	/// <param name="Converged">True if energy change between steps fell below convergence threshold.</param>
          13	/// <param name="MinimizedMolecule">Resulting 3D molecule with relaxed Cartesian coordinates.</param>
          14	public record EnergyMinimizationResult(
          15	    string Formula,
          16	    double InitialEnergyKcalPerMol,
          17	    double FinalEnergyKcalPerMol,
          18	    int Iterations,
          19	    bool Converged,
          20	    Molecule3D MinimizedMolecule
          21	);
          22
          23	/// <summary>
          24	/// Industrial-Grade Molecular Mechanics &amp; Universal Force Field (UFF) Energy Minimizer.
          25	/// Implements a full 4-term analytical potential:
          26	/// 1. Bond Stretching Energy: E_bond = Σ 0.5 * k_r * (r - r0)^2
          27	/// 2. Valence Angle Bending: E_angle = Σ 0.5 * k_θ * (θ - θ0)^2
          28	/// 3. Dihedral Torsional Strain: E_torsion = Σ 0.5 * V_n * (1 + cos(n*φ - γ))
          29	/// 4. Non-Bonded van der Waals: E_vdw = Σ ε * ((rm/r)^12 - 2*(rm/r)^6)
          30	/// Solved via Conjugate Gradient / Steepest-Descent geometric relaxation.
          31	/// </summary>
          32	public static class ForceFieldEngine
          33	{
          34	    private const double DefaultBondSpringConstant = 350.0; // kcal/(mol·Å²)
          35	    private const double DefaultAngleSpringConstant = 60.0; // kcal/(mol·rad²)
          36	    private const double DefaultTorsionBarrier = 2.5; // kcal/mol
          37	    private const double DefaultVdwEpsilon = 0.15; // kcal/mol
          38	    private const double DefaultVdwRadius = 3.4; // Å
          39
          40	    /// <summary>
          41	    /// Minimizes the total molecular mechanics potential energy of a 3D molecule.
          42	    /// </summary>
          43	    /// <param name="molecule3D">Input 3D molecular structure.</param>
          44	    /// <param name="maxIterations">Maximum optimization iterations (default: 50).</param>
          45	    /// <returns>EnergyMinimizationResult with relaxed atomic coordinates.</returns>
          46	    public static EnergyMinimizationResult MinimizeEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D, int maxIterations = 50)
          47	    {
          48	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(molecule3D);
          49
          50	        var currentPositions = molecule3D.Atoms.Select(a => a.Position).ToList();
          51	        double initialEnergy = CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, currentPositions);
          52
          53	        double energy = initialEnergy;
          54	        int iter = 0;
          55	        double stepSize = 0.02;
          56
          57	        for (iter = 0; iter < maxIterations; iter++)
          58	        {
          59	            var forces = CalculateGradients(molecule3D, currentPositions);
          60	            var newPositions = new List<Vector3D>();
          61
          62	            for (int i = 0; i < currentPositions.Count; i++)
          63	            {
          64	                var pos = currentPositions[i];
          65	                var f = forces[i];
          66	                newPositions.Add(new Vector3D(
          67	                    pos.X + f.X * stepSize,
          68	                    pos.Y + f.Y * stepSize,
          69	                    pos.Z + f.Z * stepSize
          70	                ));
          71	            }
          72
          73	            double newEnergy = CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, newPositions);
          74
          75	            if (Math.Abs(energy - newEnergy) < 1e-4)
          76	            {
          77	                energy = newEnergy;
          78	                currentPositions = newPositions;
          79	                break;
          80	            }
          81
          82	            if (newEnergy < energy)
          83	            {
          84	                energy = newEnergy;
          85	                currentPositions = newPositions;
          86	                stepSize = Math.Min(0.05, stepSize * 1.1); // Adaptive step acceleration
          87	            }
          88	            else
          89	            {
          90	                stepSize *= 0.5; // Backtrack on overshoot
          91	            }
          92	        }
          93
          94	        var minimizedAtoms = molecule3D.Atoms
          95	            .Select((a, idx) => new Atom3D(a.Atom, currentPositions[idx]))
          96	            .ToList();
          97
          98	        var minimizedMol = new Molecule3D(
          99	            molecule3D.Name,
         100	            molecule3D.ChemicalFormula,
         101	            molecule3D.VseprShape,
         102	            molecule3D.IdealBondAngleDegrees,
         103	            minimizedAtoms,
         104	            molecule3D.SourceMolecule
         105	        );
         106
         107	        return new EnergyMinimizationResult(
         108	            molecule3D.ChemicalFormula,
         109	            Math.Round(initialEnergy, 3),
         110	            Math.Round(energy, 3),
         111	            iter + 1,
         112	            true,
         113	            minimizedMol
         114	        );
         115	    }
         116
         117	    /// <summary>
         118	    /// Computes the total potential energy summing bond stretch, angle bend, dihedral, and van der Waals terms.
         119	    /// </summary>
         120	    public static double CalculateTotalEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D)
         121	    {
         122	        var positions = molecule3D.Atoms.Select(a => a.Position).ToList();
         123	        return CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, positions);
         124	    }
         125
         126	    private static double CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D, List<Vector3D> positions)
         127	    {
         128	        double eBond = 0.0;
         129	        double eAngle = 0.0;
         130	        double eTorsion = 0.0;
         131	        double eVdw = 0.0;
         132
         133	        // 1. Covalent Bond Stretching Term
         134	        foreach (var bond in molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds)
         135	        {
         136	            if (bond.Atom1Index < positions.Count && bond.Atom2Index < positions.Count)
         137	            {
         138	                double r = Distance(positions[bond.Atom1Index], positions[bond.Atom2Index]);
         139	                double r0 = GetIdealBondLength(molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Atoms[bond.Atom1Index].Element, molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Atoms[bond.Atom2Index].Element, bond.Type);
         140	                double delta = r - r0;
         141	                eBond += 0.5 * DefaultBondSpringConstant * delta * delta;
         142	            }
         143	        }
         144
         145	        // 2. Valence Angle Bending Term (Iterate connected triplets)
         146	        for (int i = 0; i < positions.Count; i++)
         147	        {
         148	            var neighbors = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         149	                .Where(b => b.Connects(i))
         150	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == i ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         151	                .ToList();
         152
         153	            double idealAngleDeg = GetIdealAngleDegrees(molecule3D.SourceMolecule, i, molecule3D.IdealBondAngleDegrees);
         154
         155	            for (int j = 0; j < neighbors.Count; j++)
         156	            {
         157	                for (int k = j + 1; k < neighbors.Count; k++)
         158	                {
         159	                    int n1 = neighbors[j];
         160	                    int n2 = neighbors[k];
         161
         162	                    double angleDeg = CalculateAngleDegrees(positions[n1], positions[i], positions[n2]);
         163	                    double angleDiffRad = (angleDeg - idealAngleDeg) * (Math.PI / 180.0);
         164	                    eAngle += 0.5 * DefaultAngleSpringConstant * angleDiffRad * angleDiffRad;
         165	                }
         166	            }
         167	        }
         168
         169	        // 3. Dihedral Torsional Strain Term (Iterate connected quartets i-j-k-l)
         170	        foreach (var centralBond in molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds)
         171	        {
         172	            int j = centralBond.Atom1Index;
         173	            int k = centralBond.Atom2Index;
         174
         175	            var jNeighbors = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         176	                .Where(b => b.Connects(j))
         177	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == j ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         178	                .Where(n => n != k)
         179	                .ToList();
         180
         181	            var kNeighbors = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         182	                .Where(b => b.Connects(k))
         183	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == k ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         184	                .Where(n => n != j)
         185	                .ToList();
         186
         187	            foreach (var i in jNeighbors)
         188	            {
         189	                foreach (var l in kNeighbors)
         190	                {
         191	                    if (i != l && i < positions.Count && j < positions.Count && k < positions.Count && l < positions.Count)
         192	                    {
         193	                        double phiRad = CalculateDihedralAngleRad(positions[i], positions[j], positions[k], positions[l]);
         194	                        // Standard 3-fold torsional barrier: E_torsion = 0.5 * V3 * (1 + cos(3*phi))
         195	                        eTorsion += 0.5 * DefaultTorsionBarrier * (1.0 + Math.Cos(3.0 * phiRad));
         196	                    }
         197	                }
         198	            }
         199	        }
         200
         201	        // 4. Non-bonded Steric van der Waals Term (12-6 Lennard-Jones)
         202	        // Standard molecular mechanics rule: 1,2 (bonded) and 1,3 (geminal/angle-connected) pairs are excluded
         203	        for (int i = 0; i < positions.Count; i++)
         204	        {
         205	            var bondedToI = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         206	                .Where(b => b.Connects(i))
         207	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == i ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         208	                .ToHashSet();
         209
         210	            // Geminal 1,3 neighbors sharing a common center atom with i
         211	            var geminalToI = new HashSet<int>();

           5	public static class SmilesParser
           6	{
           7	    private sealed record RawAtom(Element Element, int ExplicitCharge, int ExplicitH = -1, bool IsAromatic = false);
           8
           9	    public static Molecule Parse(string smiles, string? name = null)
          10	    {
          11	        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(smiles);
          12
          13	        var rawAtoms = new List<RawAtom>();
          14	        var rawBonds = new List<(int Atom1, int Atom2, BondType Type)>();
          15	        var ringOpenings = new Dictionary<int, (int AtomIndex, BondType BondType)>();
          16	        var branchStack = new Stack<int>();
          17
          18	        int currentAtomIndex = -1;
          19	        int i = 0;
          20	        int len = smiles.Length;
          21	        BondType currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          22
          23	        while (i < len)
          24	        {
          25	            char ch = smiles[i];
          26
          27	            if (ch == '(')
          28	            {
          29	                if (currentAtomIndex >= 0) branchStack.Push(currentAtomIndex);
          30	                i++;
          31	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          32	            }
          33	            else if (ch == ')')
          34	            {
          35	                if (branchStack.Count > 0) currentAtomIndex = branchStack.Pop();
          36	                i++;
          37	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          38	            }
          39	            else if (ch is '=' or '#' or ':' or '-')
          40	            {
          41	                currentBondType = ch switch
          42	                {
          43	                    '=' => BondType.Double,
          44	                    '#' => BondType.Triple,
          45	                    ':' => BondType.Aromatic,
          46	                    _ => BondType.Single
          47	                };
          48	                i++;
          49	            }
          50	            else if (char.IsDigit(ch))
          51	            {
          52	                int ringId = ch - '0';
          53	                if (ringOpenings.TryGetValue(ringId, out var open))
          54	                {
          55	                    bool bothAromatic = rawAtoms[currentAtomIndex].IsAromatic && rawAtoms[open.AtomIndex].IsAromatic;
          56	                    var ringBondType = open.BondType != BondType.Single
          57	                        ? open.BondType
          58	                        : (currentBondType != BondType.Single ? currentBondType : (bothAromatic ? BondType.Aromatic : BondType.Single));
          59	                    rawBonds.Add((open.AtomIndex, currentAtomIndex, ringBondType));
          60	                    ringOpenings.Remove(ringId);
          61	                }
          62	                else
          63	                {
          64	                    ringOpenings[ringId] = (currentAtomIndex, currentBondType);
          65	                }
          66	                i++;
          67	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          68	            }
          69	            else if (ch == '[')
          70	            {
          71	                i++;
          72	                int start = i;
          73	                while (i < len && smiles[i] != ']') i++;
          74
          75	                string bracketContent = smiles[start..i];
          76	                i++; // skip ']'
          77
          78	                var (element, charge, explicitH) = ParseBracketAtom(bracketContent);
          79	                rawAtoms.Add(new RawAtom(element, charge, explicitH, false));
          80	                int newIndex = rawAtoms.Count - 1;
          81
          82	                if (currentAtomIndex >= 0)
          83	                {
          84	                    rawBonds.Add((currentAtomIndex, newIndex, currentBondType));
          85	                }
          86
          87	                currentAtomIndex = newIndex;
          88	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          89	            }
          90	            else if (ch == '.')
          91	            {
          92	                currentAtomIndex = -1;
          93	                branchStack.Clear();
          94	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
          95	                i++;
          96	            }
          97	            else if (char.IsLetter(ch))
          98	            {
          99	                string symbol = ch.ToString();
         100	                bool isAromatic = char.IsLower(ch);
         101
         102	                if (i + 1 < len && char.IsLower(smiles[i + 1]) && !isAromatic)
         103	                {
         104	                    string candidate = smiles.Substring(i, 2);
         105	                    if (IsKnownSymbol(candidate))
         106	                    {
         107	                        symbol = candidate;
         108	                        i++;
         109	                    }
         110	                }
         111
         112	                if (isAromatic) symbol = char.ToUpper(symbol[0]).ToString();
         113
         114	                var element = Elements.GetBySymbol(symbol);
         115	                rawAtoms.Add(new RawAtom(element, 0, -1, isAromatic));
         116	                int newIndex = rawAtoms.Count - 1;
         117
         118	                if (currentAtomIndex >= 0)
         119	                {
         120	                    bool bothAromatic = isAromatic && rawAtoms[currentAtomIndex].IsAromatic;
         121	                    var bondType = currentBondType != BondType.Single
         122	                        ? currentBondType
         123	                        : (bothAromatic ? BondType.Aromatic : BondType.Single);
         124	                    rawBonds.Add((currentAtomIndex, newIndex, bondType));
         125	                }
         126
         127	                currentAtomIndex = newIndex;
         128	                currentBondType = BondType.Single;
         129	                i++;
         130	            }
         131	            else
         132	            {
         133	                i++;
         134	            }
         135	        }
         136
         137	        var finalAtoms = new List<Atom>();
         138	        var finalBonds = new List<Bond>();
         139
         140	        foreach (var bond in rawBonds)
         141	        {
         142	            finalBonds.Add(new Bond(bond.Atom1, bond.Atom2, bond.Type));
         143	        }
         144
         145	        for (int aIdx = 0; aIdx < rawAtoms.Count; aIdx++)
         146	        {
         147	            var raw = rawAtoms[aIdx];
         148	            int defaultNeutrons = Math.Max(0, (int)Math.Round(raw.Element.StandardAtomicMass) - raw.Element.AtomicNumber);
         149
         150	            var atom = new Atom(raw.Element, defaultNeutrons);
         151	            if (raw.ExplicitCharge != 0) atom = atom.Ionize(raw.ExplicitCharge);
         152
         153	            finalAtoms.Add(atom);
         154	        }
         155
         156	        int originalAtomCount = finalAtoms.Count;
         157	        for (int aIdx = 0; aIdx < originalAtomCount; aIdx++)
         158	        {
         159	            var raw = rawAtoms[aIdx];
         160	            int hCount = raw.ExplicitH;
         161
         162	            if (hCount < 0)
         163	            {
         164	                double currentBondOrder = 0;
         165	                foreach (var b in finalBonds)
         166	                {
         167	                    if (b.Connects(aIdx))
         168	                    {
         169	                        currentBondOrder += b.Type switch
         170	                        {
         171	                            BondType.Double => 2.0,
         172	                            BondType.Triple => 3.0,
         173	                            BondType.Aromatic => 1.5,
         174	                            _ => 1.0
         175	                        };
         176	                    }
         177	                }
         178
         179	                int defaultValence = GetDefaultValence(raw.Element.Symbol, currentBondOrder);
         180	                hCount = Math.Max(0, (int)Math.Round(defaultValence - currentBondOrder));
         181	            }
         182
         183	            int hDefaultNeutrons = Math.Max(0, (int)Math.Round(Elements.Hydrogen.StandardAtomicMass) - Elements.Hydrogen.AtomicNumber);
         184	            for (int h = 0; h < hCount; h++)
         185	            {
         186	                finalAtoms.Add(new Atom(Elements.Hydrogen, hDefaultNeutrons));
         187	                int hIndex = finalAtoms.Count - 1;
         188	                finalBonds.Add(new Bond(aIdx, hIndex, BondType.Single));
         189	            }
         190	        }
         191
         192	        return new Molecule(name ?? smiles, finalAtoms, finalBonds);
         193	    }

         195	    private static (Element Element, int Charge, int ExplicitH) ParseBracketAtom(string content)
         196	    {
         197	        int i = 0;
         198	        int len = content.Length;
         199
         200	        while (i < len && !char.IsLetter(content[i])) i++;
         201
         202	        int startSymbol = i;
         203	        if (i < len && char.IsUpper(content[i]))
         204	        {
         205	            i++;
         206	            if (i < len && char.IsLower(content[i])) i++;
         207	        }
         208	        else if (i < len && char.IsLower(content[i]))
         209	        {
         210	            i++;
         211	        }
         212
         213	        string symbolStr = content.Substring(startSymbol, i - startSymbol);
         214	        if (symbolStr.Length == 1 && char.IsLower(symbolStr[0])) symbolStr = char.ToUpper(symbolStr[0]).ToString();
         215
         216	        var element = Elements.GetBySymbol(symbolStr);
         217	        int explicitH = 0; // In OpenSMILES bracket atoms, hydrogen count defaults to 0 unless 'H' is specified
         218	        int charge = 0;
         219
         220	        if (i < len && (content[i] == 'H' || content[i] == 'h'))
         221	        {
         222	            i++;
         223	            int startH = i;
         224	            while (i < len && char.IsDigit(content[i])) i++;
         225	            explicitH = startH == i ? 1 : int.Parse(content.Substring(startH, i - startH));
         226	        }
         227
         228	        if (i < len && (content[i] is '+' or '-'))
         229	        {
         230	            char sign = content[i];
         231	            i++;
         232	            int startC = i;
         233	            while (i < len && char.IsDigit(content[i])) i++;
         234	            int val = startC == i ? 1 : int.Parse(content.Substring(startC, i - startC));
         235	            charge = sign == '+' ? val : -val;
         236	        }
         237
         238	        return (element, charge, explicitH);
         239	    }
         240
         241	    private static int GetDefaultValence(string symbol, double currentBondOrder) => symbol switch
         242	    {
         243	        "C" => 4,
         244	        "N" => currentBondOrder > 3.0 ? 4 : 3,
         245	        "O" => 2,
         246	        "S" => currentBondOrder > 4.0 ? 6 : (currentBondOrder > 2.0 ? 4 : 2),
         247	        "P" => currentBondOrder > 3.0 ? 5 : 3,
         248	        "F" or "Cl" or "Br" or "I" => 1,
         249	        _ => 0
         250	    };
         251
         252	    public static bool TryParse(string smiles, [System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.NotNullWhen(true)] out Molecule? molecule) =>
         253	        TryParse(smiles, null, out molecule, out _);
         254
         255	    public static bool TryParse(string smiles, string? name, [System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.NotNullWhen(true)] out Molecule? molecule, out string? errorMessage)
         256	    {
         257	        molecule = null;
         258	        errorMessage = null;
         259	        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(smiles))
         260	        {
         261	            errorMessage = "SMILES string cannot be null or whitespace.";
         262	            return false;
         263	        }
         264
         265	        try
         266	        {
         267	            molecule = Parse(smiles, name);
         268	            return true;
         269	        }
         270	        catch (Exception ex)
         271	        {
         272	            errorMessage = ex.Message;
         273	            return false;
         274	        }
         275	    }
         276
         277	    private static bool IsKnownSymbol(string symbol) => Elements.TryGetBySymbol(symbol, out _);
         278	}

          56	## 💡 What is Chemy?
          57
          58	**Chemy** is a modern, high-performance computational chemistry platform built for developers, scientists, students, and pharmaceutical researchers.
          59
          60	All algorithms in Chemy are **pure, mathematically rigorous, and deterministic C# implementations** without external Python, cloud AI, or black-box dependencies:
          61	- ⚛️ **Quantum Electronic Structure & Hückel Molecular Orbitals**: Solves the secular equation $\det|\mathbf{H} - E\mathbf{I}| = 0$ via exact Jacobi symmetric matrix diagonalization. Computes HOMO, LUMO, bandgaps, UV-Vis $\lambda_{\max}$, Dewar aromatic resonance energy, Coulson bond orders, and Fukui reactivity indices (`HuckelEngine`).
          62	- 🌿 **Chemical Graph Theory & Subgraph Isomorphism**: Implements subgraph matching (`SubgraphMatcher`) and topological graph rewriting (`GraphRewriter`) on immutable molecular graphs (`ChemicalGraph`).
          63	- ⚛️ **Multi-Term Molecular Mechanics Force Field**: 4-term analytical potential (Bond Stretching, Hybridization Angle Bending, Dihedral Torsions, 12-6 Lennard-Jones van der Waals) with **exact analytical gradients** ($-\nabla E$) and geometric energy relaxation (`ForceFieldEngine`).
          64	- 📐 **3D Multi-Center Conformer Embedding**: Generates physically valid 3D Cartesian coordinates for branched and cyclic molecules via topological coordinate propagation and VSEPR coordinate frames (`Geometry3DEngine`).
          65	- 🛡️ **Published Chemoinformatics & ADMET Standards**: Atom-additive Wildman-Crippen $\log P$, 43-fragment Ertl Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA), Bickerton QED drug-likeness desirability functions, Lipinski Rule of 5, Veber Oral Bioavailability rules, and Ghose filters (`AdmetEngine`).
          66	- 🧬 **Bioisosteric Lead Optimization**: Evaluates lead candidates across generations optimizing QED and $\log P$ while replacing metabolic liabilities via bioisosteric graph mutation operators (`MolecularEvolverEngine`).
          67	- ⚖️ **Exact Mass & Redox Charge Balancer**: Solves chemical equations using exact rational Gaussian elimination nullspace matrix algebra ($M\vec{x} = \vec{0}$) over $\mathbb{Q}$ with dedicated net electrostatic charge conservation (`Reaction`).
          68	- 💧 **Exact Weak Electrolyte Cubic Equilibria**: Solves exact polynomial equilibrium equations ($[\text{H}^+]^3 + K_a [\text{H}^+]^2 - (K_w + K_a C)[\text{H}^+] - K_a K_w = 0$) via Halley's method across arbitrary dilution regimes (`SolutionsEngine`).
          69	- 🔥 **True Benson Group Additivity**: Graph-based Benson group increment estimation for standard enthalpy ($\Delta H_f^\circ$), entropy ($S^\circ$), and Gibbs free energy ($\Delta G^\circ$) with ring strain corrections (`ThermodynamicsEngine`).
          70	- ♻️ **EcoClean PFAS & Plastic Degradation Pathways**: Models topological Bond Dissociation Energies ($\text{BDE}$) and constructs enzymatic/electrochemical catalytic degradation cascades for persistent pollutants (`EcoCleanEngine`).
          71	- 📉 **Empirical Spectroscopy Predictor**: Predicts $^1\text{H}$-NMR, $^{13}\text{C}$-NMR chemical shifts, and IR vibrational absorption bands across 12+ organic functional group classes (`SpectroscopyEngine`).
          72	- ⏱️ **Arbitrary Reaction Network RK4 Solver**: 4th-Order Runge-Kutta numerical differential integrator for multi-species chemical kinetics networks (`ReactionNetworkEngine`).
          73	- 📁 **Standard Chemical File Exporter**: Full support for MDL Molfile (V2000), Structure-Data Files (SDF), Protein Data Bank (PDB), and XYZ formats (`MolfileExporter`).
          74	- 🌐 **NCBI PubChem Integrator**: Live REST query client for 110M+ real compounds.

          35	    private const double DefaultAngleSpringConstant = 60.0; // kcal/(mol·rad²)
          36	    private const double DefaultTorsionBarrier = 2.5; // kcal/mol
          37	    private const double DefaultVdwEpsilon = 0.15; // kcal/mol
          38	    private const double DefaultVdwRadius = 3.4; // Å
          39
          40	    /// <summary>
          41	    /// Minimizes the total molecular mechanics potential energy of a 3D molecule.
          42	    /// </summary>
          43	    /// <param name="molecule3D">Input 3D molecular structure.</param>
          44	    /// <param name="maxIterations">Maximum optimization iterations (default: 50).</param>
          45	    /// <returns>EnergyMinimizationResult with relaxed atomic coordinates.</returns>
          46	    public static EnergyMinimizationResult MinimizeEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D, int maxIterations = 50)
          47	    {
          48	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(molecule3D);
          49
          50	        var currentPositions = molecule3D.Atoms.Select(a => a.Position).ToList();
          51	        double initialEnergy = CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, currentPositions);
          52
          53	        double energy = initialEnergy;
          54	        int iter = 0;
          55	        double stepSize = 0.02;
          56
          57	        for (iter = 0; iter < maxIterations; iter++)
          58	        {
          59	            var forces = CalculateGradients(molecule3D, currentPositions);
          60	            var newPositions = new List<Vector3D>();
          61
          62	            for (int i = 0; i < currentPositions.Count; i++)
          63	            {
          64	                var pos = currentPositions[i];
          65	                var f = forces[i];
          66	                newPositions.Add(new Vector3D(
          67	                    pos.X + f.X * stepSize,
          68	                    pos.Y + f.Y * stepSize,
          69	                    pos.Z + f.Z * stepSize
          70	                ));
          71	            }
          72
          73	            double newEnergy = CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, newPositions);
          74
          75	            if (Math.Abs(energy - newEnergy) < 1e-4)
          76	            {
          77	                energy = newEnergy;
          78	                currentPositions = newPositions;
          79	                break;
          80	            }
          81
          82	            if (newEnergy < energy)
          83	            {
          84	                energy = newEnergy;
          85	                currentPositions = newPositions;
          86	                stepSize = Math.Min(0.05, stepSize * 1.1); // Adaptive step acceleration
          87	            }
          88	            else
          89	            {
          90	                stepSize *= 0.5; // Backtrack on overshoot
          91	            }
          92	        }
          93
          94	        var minimizedAtoms = molecule3D.Atoms
          95	            .Select((a, idx) => new Atom3D(a.Atom, currentPositions[idx]))
          96	            .ToList();
          97
          98	        var minimizedMol = new Molecule3D(
          99	            molecule3D.Name,
         100	            molecule3D.ChemicalFormula,
         101	            molecule3D.VseprShape,
         102	            molecule3D.IdealBondAngleDegrees,
         103	            minimizedAtoms,
         104	            molecule3D.SourceMolecule
         105	        );
         106
         107	        return new EnergyMinimizationResult(
         108	            molecule3D.ChemicalFormula,
         109	            Math.Round(initialEnergy, 3),
         110	            Math.Round(energy, 3),
         111	            iter + 1,
         112	            true,
         113	            minimizedMol
         114	        );
         115	    }
         116
         117	    /// <summary>
         118	    /// Computes the total potential energy summing bond stretch, angle bend, dihedral, and van der Waals terms.
         119	    /// </summary>
         120	    public static double CalculateTotalEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D)
         121	    {
         122	        var positions = molecule3D.Atoms.Select(a => a.Position).ToList();
         123	        return CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(molecule3D, positions);
         124	    }
         125
         126	    private static double CalculateTotalPotentialEnergy(Molecule3D molecule3D, List<Vector3D> positions)
         127	    {
         128	        double eBond = 0.0;
         129	        double eAngle = 0.0;
         130	        double eTorsion = 0.0;
         131	        double eVdw = 0.0;
         132
         133	        // 1. Covalent Bond Stretching Term
         134	        foreach (var bond in molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds)
         135	        {
         136	            if (bond.Atom1Index < positions.Count && bond.Atom2Index < positions.Count)
         137	            {
         138	                double r = Distance(positions[bond.Atom1Index], positions[bond.Atom2Index]);
         139	                double r0 = GetIdealBondLength(molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Atoms[bond.Atom1Index].Element, molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Atoms[bond.Atom2Index].Element, bond.Type);
         140	                double delta = r - r0;
         141	                eBond += 0.5 * DefaultBondSpringConstant * delta * delta;
         142	            }
         143	        }
         144
         145	        // 2. Valence Angle Bending Term (Iterate connected triplets)
         146	        for (int i = 0; i < positions.Count; i++)
         147	        {
         148	            var neighbors = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         149	                .Where(b => b.Connects(i))
         150	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == i ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         151	                .ToList();
         152
         153	            double idealAngleDeg = GetIdealAngleDegrees(molecule3D.SourceMolecule, i, molecule3D.IdealBondAngleDegrees);
         154
         155	            for (int j = 0; j < neighbors.Count; j++)
         156	            {
         157	                for (int k = j + 1; k < neighbors.Count; k++)
         158	                {
         159	                    int n1 = neighbors[j];
         160	                    int n2 = neighbors[k];
         161
         162	                    double angleDeg = CalculateAngleDegrees(positions[n1], positions[i], positions[n2]);
         163	                    double angleDiffRad = (angleDeg - idealAngleDeg) * (Math.PI / 180.0);
         164	                    eAngle += 0.5 * DefaultAngleSpringConstant * angleDiffRad * angleDiffRad;
         165	                }
         166	            }
         167	        }
         168
         169	        // 3. Dihedral Torsional Strain Term (Iterate connected quartets i-j-k-l)
         170	        foreach (var centralBond in molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds)
         171	        {
         172	            int j = centralBond.Atom1Index;
         173	            int k = centralBond.Atom2Index;
         174
         175	            var jNeighbors = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         176	                .Where(b => b.Connects(j))
         177	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == j ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         178	                .Where(n => n != k)
         179	                .ToList();
         180
         388	        }
         389
         390	        // 4. van der Waals 12-6 Lennard Jones forces (1,4+ non-bonded)
         391	        for (int i = 0; i < nAtoms; i++)
         392	        {
         393	            var bondedToI = molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds
         394	                .Where(b => b.Connects(i))
         395	                .Select(b => b.Atom1Index == i ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index)
         396	                .ToHashSet();
         397
         398	            for (int j = i + 1; j < nAtoms; j++)
         399	            {
         400	                if (bondedToI.Contains(j)) continue;
         401
         402	                var p1 = positions[i];
         403	                var p2 = positions[j];
         404	                double dist = Math.Max(0.8, Distance(p1, p2));
         405
         406	                if (dist < DefaultVdwRadius * 1.8)
         407	                {
         408	                    double ratio = DefaultVdwRadius / dist;
         409	                    double term6 = Math.Pow(ratio, 6);
         410	                    double term12 = term6 * term6;
         411	                    // Analytical gradient of Lennard-Jones: dE/dr = 12*eps/r * (term6 - term12)
         412	                    double vdwForce = DefaultVdwEpsilon * 12.0 * (term12 - term6) / (dist * dist);
         413	                    vdwForce = Math.Clamp(vdwForce, -0.2, 0.2);
         414
         415	                    double fvX = ((p1.X - p2.X) / dist) * vdwForce;
         416	                    double fvY = ((p1.Y - p2.Y) / dist) * vdwForce;
         417	                    double fvZ = ((p1.Z - p2.Z) / dist) * vdwForce;
         418
         419	                    fx[i] += fvX; fy[i] += fvY; fz[i] += fvZ;
         420	                    fx[j] -= fvX; fy[j] -= fvY; fz[j] -= fvZ;
         421	                }
         422	            }
         423	        }
         424
         425	        for (int i = 0; i < nAtoms; i++)
         426	        {
         427	            forces.Add(new Vector3D(fx[i], fy[i], fz[i]));
         428	        }
         429
         430	        return forces;

         145	    /// <summary>
         146	    /// Calculates Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA) using standard Ertl atomic fragment contributions.
         147	    /// Reference: Ertl et al., J. Med. Chem. 2000, 43, 3714-3717.
         148	    /// </summary>
         149	    public static double CalculateErtlTpsa(Molecule molecule)
         150	    {
         151	        double tpsa = 0.0;
         152	        int nAtoms = molecule.Atoms.Count;
         153
         154	        for (int i = 0; i < nAtoms; i++)
         155	        {
         156	            var atom = molecule.Atoms[i];
         157	            string sym = atom.Element.Symbol;
         158
         159	            if (sym == "O")
         160	            {
         161	                var bonded = GetNeighborIndices(molecule, i);
         162	                int hCount = bonded.Count(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "H");
         163	                bool isDouble = molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Connects(i) && b.Type == BondType.Double);
         164	                bool bondedToCarbonyl = bonded.Any(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "C" &&
         165	                    molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Connects(idx) && b.Type == BondType.Double && molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index == idx ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol == "O"));
         166
         167	                if (isDouble)
         168	                {
         169	                    tpsa += 17.07; // Carbonyl / Nitro / Sulfone =O
         170	                }
         171	                else if (hCount > 0)
         172	                {
         173	                    tpsa += 20.23; // Hydroxyl -OH
         174	                }
         175	                else if (bondedToCarbonyl)
         176	                {
         177	                    tpsa += 9.23; // Ester bridging -O-
         178	                }
         179	                else
         180	                {
         181	                    tpsa += 9.23; // Ether -O-
         182	                }
         183	            }
         184	            else if (sym == "N")
         185	            {
         186	                var bonded = GetNeighborIndices(molecule, i);
         187	                int hCount = bonded.Count(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "H");
         188	                int nonHCount = bonded.Count - hCount;
         189	                bool isAromatic = molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Connects(i) && b.Type == BondType.Aromatic);
         190	                bool isTriple = molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Connects(i) && b.Type == BondType.Triple);
         191	                bool isAmide = bonded.Any(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "C" &&
         192	                    molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Connects(idx) && b.Type == BondType.Double && molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index == idx ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol == "O"));
         193	                int oCount = bonded.Count(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "O");
         194
         195	                if (oCount >= 2)
         196	                {
         197	                    tpsa += 45.82; // Nitro -NO2 group
         198	                }
         199	                else if (isTriple)
         200	                {
         201	                    tpsa += 23.79; // Nitrile -C≡N
         202	                }
         203	                else if (isAmide)
         204	                {
         205	                    tpsa += hCount switch
         206	                    {
         207	                        >= 2 => 43.09, // Primary amide -CONH2
         208	                        1 => 29.10,    // Secondary amide -CONHR
         209	                        _ => 20.31     // Tertiary amide -CONR2
         210	                    };
         211	                }
         212	                else if (isAromatic)
         213	                {
         214	                    tpsa += hCount switch
         215	                    {
         216	                        >= 1 => 15.79, // Aromatic -NH- (pyrrole/indole)
         217	                        _ => 12.89     // Pyridyl =N-
         218	                    };
         219	                }
         220	                else
         221	                {
         222	                    tpsa += hCount switch
         223	                    {
         224	                        >= 2 => 26.02, // Primary aliphatic amine -NH2
         225	                        1 => 12.03,    // Secondary aliphatic amine -NH-
         226	                        _ => 3.24      // Tertiary aliphatic amine -NR2
         227	                    };
         228	                }
         229	            }
         230	            else if (sym == "S")
         231	            {
         232	                var bonded = GetNeighborIndices(molecule, i);
         233	                int oCount = bonded.Count(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "O");
         234	                int hCount = bonded.Count(idx => molecule.Atoms[idx].Element.Symbol == "H");
         235
         236	                if (oCount >= 1) tpsa += 28.24; // Sulfoxide / Sulfone
         237	                else if (hCount > 0) tpsa += 38.80; // Thiol -SH
         238	                else tpsa += 25.30; // Thioether -S-
         239	            }
         240	            else if (sym == "P")
         241	            {
         242	                tpsa += 9.81; // Phosphate polar surface
         243	            }
         244	        }
         245
         246	        return Math.Round(tpsa, 1);
         247	    }

         433	    private static int CountRotatableBonds(Molecule molecule)
         434	    {
         435	        int rotatable = 0;
         436	        foreach (var bond in molecule.Bonds)
         437	        {
         438	            if (bond.Type == BondType.Single)
         439	            {
         440	                var e1 = molecule.Atoms[bond.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol;
         441	                var e2 = molecule.Atoms[bond.Atom2Index].Element.Symbol;
         442
         443	                // Non-terminal bonds (neither atom is H or Halogen) and NOT in a cyclic ring
         444	                if (e1 != "H" && e2 != "H" && e1 != "F" && e2 != "F" && e1 != "Cl" && e2 != "Cl" && e1 != "Br" && e2 != "Br")
         445	                {
         446	                    if (!IsBondInRing(molecule, bond))
         447	                    {
         448	                        int heavyDeg1 = molecule.Bonds.Count(b => b.Connects(bond.Atom1Index) && molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index == bond.Atom1Index ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol != "H");
         449	                        int heavyDeg2 = molecule.Bonds.Count(b => b.Connects(bond.Atom2Index) && molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index == bond.Atom2Index ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol != "H");
         450	                        if (heavyDeg1 > 1 && heavyDeg2 > 1) rotatable++;
         451	                    }
         452	                }
         453	            }
         454	        }
         455	        return Math.Max(0, rotatable);
         456	    }
         457
         458	    private static bool IsBondInRing(Molecule molecule, Bond bond)
         459	    {
         460	        int start = bond.Atom1Index;
         461	        int target = bond.Atom2Index;
         462
         463	        var visited = new HashSet<int> { start };
         464	        var queue = new Queue<int>();
         465
         466	        foreach (var b in molecule.Bonds)
         467	        {
         468	            if (b == bond) continue;
         469	            if (b.Connects(start))
         470	            {
         471	                int neighbor = b.Atom1Index == start ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index;
         472	                if (neighbor == target) return true;
         473	                visited.Add(neighbor);
         474	                queue.Enqueue(neighbor);
         475	            }
         476	        }
         477
         478	        while (queue.Count > 0)
         479	        {
         480	            int current = queue.Dequeue();
         481	            if (current == target) return true;
         482
         483	            foreach (var b in molecule.Bonds)
         484	            {
         485	                if (b == bond) continue;
         486	                if (b.Connects(current))
         487	                {
         488	                    int neighbor = b.Atom1Index == current ? b.Atom2Index : b.Atom1Index;
         489	                    if (!visited.Contains(neighbor))
         490	                    {
         491	                        visited.Add(neighbor);
         492	                        queue.Enqueue(neighbor);
         493	                    }
         494	                }
         495	            }
         496	        }
         497
         498	        return false;
         499	    }
         500
         501	    private static int CountAromaticRings(Molecule molecule)
         502	    {
         503	        var graph = Graph.ChemicalGraph.FromMolecule(molecule);
         504	        var rings = graph.FindRings();
         505	        int count = 0;
         506	        foreach (var ring in rings)
         507	        {
         508	            bool hasAromatic = ring.Any(nodeId => graph.GetIncidentEdges(nodeId).Any(e => e.IsAromatic || e.BondType == BondType.Aromatic));
         509	            if (hasAromatic && ring.Count is 5 or 6)
         510	            {
         511	                count++;
         512	            }
         513	        }
         514	        return Math.Max(count, molecule.Bonds.Any(b => b.Type == BondType.Aromatic) ? 1 : 0);
         515	    }

         517	    private static int CountStructuralAlerts(Molecule molecule)
         518	    {
         519	        // Counts reactive toxicophores (PAINS / Brenk filter alerts)
         520	        int alerts = 0;
         521	        var fgs = molecule.GetFunctionalGroups();
         522
         523	        // 1. Reactive Halides
         524	        bool hasAlkylHalide = molecule.Bonds.Any(b =>
         525	        {
         526	            string e1 = molecule.Atoms[b.Atom1Index].Element.Symbol;
         527	            string e2 = molecule.Atoms[b.Atom2Index].Element.Symbol;
         528	            return (e1 == "C" && e2 is "Cl" or "Br" or "I") || (e2 == "C" && e1 is "Cl" or "Br" or "I");
         529	        });
         530	        if (hasAlkylHalide && !fgs.Contains(FunctionalGroup.Aromatic)) alerts++;
         531
         532	        // 2. Nitro groups
         533	        if (fgs.Contains(FunctionalGroup.Nitro)) alerts++;
         534
         535	        // 3. Reactive aldehydes
         536	        if (fgs.Contains(FunctionalGroup.Aldehyde)) alerts++;
         537
         538	        return alerts;
         539	    }

         541	    private static double CalculateQedScore(double mw, double logP, double tpsa, int hbd, int hba, int rot, int rings, int alerts = 0)
         542	    {
         543	        // Exact Bickerton et al. (Nature Chemistry 2012, 4, 90-98) asymmetric desirability functions
         544	        // d(x) = a + b / (1 + exp(-(x - c) / d))
         545	        double dMw = AsymmetricDesirability(mw, 0.0, 1.05, 381.9, -123.6);
         546	        double dLogP = AsymmetricDesirability(logP, 0.0, 1.03, 2.83, -1.33);
         547	        double dHbd = AsymmetricDesirability(hbd, 0.0, 1.05, 1.86, -1.20);
         548	        double dHba = AsymmetricDesirability(hba, 0.0, 1.05, 4.38, -2.21);
         549	        double dTpsa = AsymmetricDesirability(tpsa, 0.0, 1.05, 68.2, -37.8);
         550	        double dRot = AsymmetricDesirability(rot, 0.0, 1.06, 4.77, -2.72);
         551	        double dArom = AsymmetricDesirability(rings, 0.0, 1.05, 1.65, -1.01);
         552	        double dAlerts = AsymmetricDesirability(alerts, 0.0, 1.06, 0.48, -0.61);
         553
         554	        // Published parameter weights: MW, LogP, HBD, HBA, TPSA, ROTB, AROM, ALERTS
         555	        double[] weights = [0.66, 0.46, 0.61, 0.05, 0.65, 0.48, 0.95, 0.77];
         556	        double[] dScores = [dMw, dLogP, dHbd, dHba, dTpsa, dRot, dArom, dAlerts];
         557
         558	        double sumWeightedLog = 0.0;
         559	        double sumWeights = 0.0;
         560
         561	        for (int i = 0; i < weights.Length; i++)
         562	        {
         563	            double dClamped = Math.Clamp(dScores[i], 1e-4, 1.0);
         564	            sumWeightedLog += weights[i] * Math.Log(dClamped);
         565	            sumWeights += weights[i];
         566	        }
         567
         568	        double qed = Math.Exp(sumWeightedLog / sumWeights);
         569	        return Math.Clamp(qed, 0.05, 0.98);
         570	    }
         571
         572	    private static double AsymmetricDesirability(double x, double a, double b, double c, double d)
         573	    {
         574	        double exponent = -(x - c) / d;
         575	        if (exponent > 50.0) return a;
         576	        if (exponent < -50.0) return a + b;
         577	        return a + (b / (1.0 + Math.Exp(exponent)));
         578	    }

      docs/SCIENTIFIC_VERIFICATION_BENCHMARKS.md:38:* **Theory**: Element masses are based on IUPAC Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights (CIAAW).
      docs/SCIENTIFIC_VERIFICATION_BENCHMARKS.md:79:* **Physical Theory**: Gillespie-Nyholm Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory states that 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs on Oxygen form an $AX_2E_2$ tetrahedral electron domain geometry compressed by lone-pair repulsion to a $104.5^\circ$ bond angle and $0.96\text{ \AA}$ $\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond length.

         248	        foreach (var b in molecule3D.SourceMolecule.Bonds)

         263	                double dy = ((p1.Y - p2.Y) / r) * springForce;

# Credibility assessment

Verdict: **Chemy is a promising educational/prototyping chemistry library, but it is not currently credible as an industrial or research-grade scientific tool.**

My assessment:

| Intended use | Credibility |
|---|---:|
| Chemistry education and demonstrations | Moderate |
| Developer prototyping | Moderate |
| Routine quantitative scientific analysis | Low |
| Drug-safety or environmental decisions | Very low |
| Published/reproducible research without independent validation | Not recommended |

The repository’s claimed **9.5/10 scientific credibility and “100% verified” badge are not supported by the available evidence**. A defensible overall rating is approximately **4/10**, with individual components ranging from reasonably sound textbook calculations to unsupported predictive outputs.

## Strong points

- The project is organized clearly and has readable, documented C# code.
- The test suite genuinely passes: **114 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, in 146 ms.
- Some foundational functionality appears appropriate for educational or utility use:
  - formula parsing and molecular-mass calculation;
  - common reaction balancing;
  - Nernst, Arrhenius, Hess-law, and buffer calculations;
  - RK4 integration;
  - Hückel calculations for small, conventional conjugated systems;
  - SVG and molecular-file generation.
- Limitations such as heuristic conformers and lack of stereochemical handling are at least mentioned in parts of the documentation.

These are useful engineering foundations, but they do not validate the broader scientific claims.

## Major credibility problems

### 1. Environmental predictions are manufactured, not scientifically calculated

The PFAS “mineralization efficiency” is generated from:

```csharp
99.0 + Clamp(10.0 / secondaryBde, 0.2, 0.8)
```

See [EcoCleanEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Environmental/EcoCleanEngine.cs:256).

There is no kinetic model, experimental calibration, reaction stoichiometry, uncertainty analysis, environmental conditions, catalyst loading, or mass-balance calculation behind this percentage. The code also appends “100% Mineralized” text regardless of demonstrated conversion.

The only dedicated test checks that the result is above 90%—essentially confirming the hard-coded behavior rather than validating it experimentally: [EcoCleanTests.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core.Tests/EcoCleanTests.cs:8).

This makes claims such as “99.4% PFAS mineralization” scientifically unsafe.

### 2. ADMET output is presented with too much authority

The system labels molecules with statements such as:

- “Low Risk (Normal cardiac safety window)”
- “High BBB Permeability”
- CYP enzyme assignments
- hERG cardiac risk

These are produced by a few fixed thresholds and functional-group checks, not validated QSAR models: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:80).

The hydrogen-bond acceptor implementation simply counts every O, N, and F atom: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:430). That incorrectly handles common cases such as amide nitrogen, protonated nitrogen, pyrrolic nitrogen, acids, and covalently bound fluorine.

Consequently, this should be described as a **rule-based descriptor demo**, not an ADMET or safety predictor.

### 3. The claimed published descriptor implementations are incomplete

The documentation says the complete 43-fragment Ertl TPSA scheme is implemented. The code instead uses a much smaller decision tree with coarse fragment categories: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:149).

There is also a direct benchmark inconsistency:

- The code assigns a carboxylic acid `17.07 + 20.23 = 37.3 Å²`.
- The benchmark document says this somehow gives `34.1 Å²`: [SCIENTIFIC_VERIFICATION_BENCHMARKS.md](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/docs/SCIENTIFIC_VERIFICATION_BENCHMARKS.md:207).

The QED calculation similarly uses simplified sigmoid functions rather than a demonstrated reproduction of the published QED implementation: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:541).

### 4. The force-field implementation contradicts its “exact gradient” claim

The energy calculation excludes both 1–2 and 1–3 nonbonded pairs. However, the force calculation only excludes directly bonded 1–2 pairs: [ForceFieldEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Physics/ForceFieldEngine.cs:390).

Therefore, the calculated forces are not the exact gradient of the energy being minimized. Additional arbitrary scale factors and force clamping further contradict the “exact analytical gradients” description.

More seriously, `MinimizeEnergy` returns `Converged = true` unconditionally, even when the iteration limit is reached: [ForceFieldEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Physics/ForceFieldEngine.cs:107).

The corresponding tests only verify nonnegative energy and the hard-coded convergence flag; they do not validate gradients, known minima, bond lengths, conformer ordering, or energy conservation: [ForceFieldTests.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core.Tests/ForceFieldTests.cs:9).

### 5. Passing tests are being confused with scientific validation

The 114 tests are useful regression tests, but many assertions are permissive—for example, accepting a broad TPSA range or merely requiring a result to be nonnegative. They mostly compare the implementation against expected values chosen within the same repository.

Missing validation evidence includes:

- comparison against independent reference implementations such as RDKit or established quantum/force-field packages;
- large benchmark datasets;
- error distributions such as MAE/RMSE;
- train/test or calibration separation;
- uncertainty estimates;
- property-based and fuzz testing;
- numerical convergence studies;
- external replication;
- test coverage reporting;
- continuous integration configuration.

The “verification report” appears to be a self-assessment, not an independent audit: [SCIENTIFIC_CREDIBILITY_REPORT.md](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/docs/SCIENTIFIC_CREDIBILITY_REPORT.md:1).

### 6. Documentation contains demonstrably inaccurate engineering claims

The README says warnings are treated as errors: [README.md](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/README.md:249).

The actual configuration explicitly says:

```xml
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

See [Directory.Build.props](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Directory.Build.props:5).

The README also displays an MIT license badge, but no license file is present in the repository. Claims such as “zero allocations,” “ISO/IUPAC-compliant MDL Molfile,” and “industrial-grade” are not backed by benchmarks, conformance suites, or certification.

## Recommended use today

Chemy is suitable for:

- teaching textbook chemistry equations;
- demonstrating graph, numerical, and cheminformatics concepts;
- building UI/API prototypes;
- exploratory calculations that will be independently checked.

It should not currently be used to:

- assess drug safety, hERG risk, BBB penetration, or metabolic pathways;
- recommend lead compounds;
- predict experimental spectra quantitatively;
- design PFAS remediation;
- rank molecular conformers or energies;
- generate research results without verification against trusted software and experimental data.

## What would make it credible

The highest-priority changes are:

1. Remove “industrial-grade,” “100% verified,” “safety,” and 9.5/10 claims until independently demonstrated.
2. Label every output by evidence level: exact algebra, numerical approximation, empirical descriptor, heuristic, or unsupported rule.
3. Remove fabricated mineralization efficiencies and categorical medical-safety language.
4. Validate descriptors molecule-by-molecule against an established reference implementation over a public benchmark dataset.
5. Correct the force/energy inconsistency and test gradients with finite-difference checks.
6. Add reference datasets, scripts that regenerate benchmark tables, error metrics, CI, coverage, versioned results, citations with DOI links, `LICENSE`, and `CITATION.cff`.
7. Make unsupported SMILES syntax fail explicitly instead of silently accepting or ignoring it.
8. Obtain review from computational chemists for each scientific subsystem.

In short: **the code demonstrates genuine effort and contains useful textbook functionality, but the marketing and scientific conclusions substantially exceed what the implementation and tests establish.**

## User

Have you analysed the code to check if the code does what the documentation claims?

## Assistant

Yes—but as a **targeted source-code audit**, not a complete line-by-line verification of every engine.

I compared several high-impact documentation claims directly against their implementations and tests. That produced concrete contradictions:

- **Force field:** documentation claims exact analytical gradients with 1–2 and 1–3 exclusions. Energy excludes both, but gradient calculation excludes only 1–2 pairs: [ForceFieldEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Physics/ForceFieldEngine.cs:390). It also reports `Converged = true` unconditionally: [ForceFieldEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Physics/ForceFieldEngine.cs:107).
- **Ertl TPSA:** documentation claims the full 43-fragment method, but the implementation is a small heuristic decision tree: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:149). Its carboxylic-acid calculation conflicts with the documented ibuprofen result.
- **ADMET:** documented safety predictions are actually fixed thresholds and functional-group rules, not validated predictive models: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:80). Hydrogen-bond acceptors are simplistically counted as every O, N, or F: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:430).
- **QED:** the implementation uses simplified sigmoid parameters rather than demonstrating a faithful reproduction of the complete published method: [AdmetEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Pharmacology/AdmetEngine.cs:541).
- **EcoClean:** its reported 99%+ mineralization efficiency is generated from a fixed arithmetic formula, not a degradation or kinetic model: [EcoCleanEngine.cs](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Chemy.Core/Environmental/EcoCleanEngine.cs:256).
- **Build quality:** documentation says warnings are treated as errors, while configuration explicitly disables that: [Directory.Build.props](/Users/moura/Desktop/chemy/src/Directory.Build.props:5).
- **Tests:** I ran the complete suite—114 tests passed—but inspected representative tests and found that several establish execution/regression behavior rather than independent scientific validity.

I also inspected the SMILES parser, Hückel implementation and tests, thermodynamics, environmental engine, force field, pharmacology engine, benchmark report, scientific approach, and credibility report.

What I have **not yet done** is formally audit every algorithm and every documented claim—for example, proving the reaction nullspace solver for edge cases, independently reproducing every Hückel result, checking all thermodynamic constants against primary sources, or validating every file exporter against external conformance tools. So the earlier report is a defensible repository-level assessment, but not a complete scientific verification audit.

## User

So, how can you afirm such a thing without having a clear picture on what the code does?

## Assistant

You’re right. I overstated the scope and certainty of my assessment.

I had enough evidence to say that **some prominent documentation claims are contradicted by the code**—for example, unconditional force-field convergence, inconsistent nonbonded exclusions, heuristic mineralization percentages, and warnings-as-errors being disabled. A single verified contradiction is sufficient to reject a global claim like “100% scientifically verified.”

But that evidence was **not sufficient** to assign the entire project an overall 4/10 rating or confidently characterize every subsystem. That requires a systematic audit of all engines, their numerical behavior, reference data, tests, API behavior, and documentation claims. I should have separated:

- Confirmed discrepancies found in inspected components.
- Components that appeared plausible but were not independently validated.
- Components I had not examined sufficiently.
- The limited conclusion supported by those findings.

The accurate conclusion should have been:

> “The repository’s blanket credibility claims are not currently substantiated, and several inspected claims are demonstrably inaccurate. A complete judgment about the scientific correctness of the entire tool requires a broader component-by-component audit.”

So yes: my specific findings remain valid, but my repository-wide score and some categorical conclusions were premature. I should not have presented a targeted audit as a comprehensive assessment.

         147	    /// <summary>

         152	    /// <exception cref="KeyNotFoundException">Thrown if symbol is not found.</exception>
         153	    public static Element GetBySymbol(string symbol) =>

         156	            : throw new KeyNotFoundException($"No element found with symbol '{symbol}'.");
